pages.text: A pit kiln is an early way to $(l:core_mechanics/heating)heat$() things, for example to $(thing)fire$() clay into ceramic. Over about $(cfg:pitKilnTicks) it heats what lies in it, but only to about 900 °C: a heap of straw and logs without a draught gets no hotter.$(br2)That is enough for clay ware (850 °C), and not for fire clay ware (1300 °C) or for melting copper (1080 °C).

To build a pit kiln you need:$(li)up to four items to fire$(li)eight pieces of $(thing)Straw$()$(li)eight $(thing)Logs$()$(li)something to light a fire, a $(l:getting_started/firepit#firestarter)Firestarter$() or a $(thing)Torch$().$(br2)$(bold)Note:$() a torch thrown on the kiln lights it within seconds.

$(bold)1.$() Put up to four items into a hole one block wide with $(item)$(k:tfc.key.place_block)$().$(br)$(bold)2.$() Cover them with eight $(thing)Straw$() or two $(thing)Thatch$() blocks.$(br)$(bold)3.$() Fill the pit with eight $(thing)Logs$().$(br)$(bold)4.$() Light the top.$(br2)The kiln burns for $(cfg:pitKilnTicks) and slowly heats what is inside. It makes smoke and carbon monoxide: see $(l:tfcpp/gases#fires)Gases$() and $(l:tfcpp/poisons#carbon_monoxide)Poisons$().

$(li)Clay ware, molds, bricks, terracotta: yes, at 850 °C.$(li)Fire clay ware: no. It needs 1300 °C, see $(l:metalworking/fire_clay)Fire Clay$().$(li)Copper, gold, silver, brass, bronze: they do not melt here. Tin, bismuth, zinc and lead do. A metal item that would melt is left as it was.$(li)The kiln reaches 900 °C after about two thirds of its burning time.
